# A04 report: the writer

Branch `v2-a04-writer`. `npm run typecheck` is clean and `npm run selfcheck`
passes (217 checks, 1 skipped by the v1 suite). A04's 62 checks are in
`scripts/checks/a04-writer.ts`.

## Acceptance

- ✅ **Every sent letter has critic ≥ 8, a lint pass and a clean truth lock (enforced in code).**
  `writeApplication` saves an application as written only after `assertGates()` passes on the exact saved text:
  - the critic score is at least 8;
  - every lint check passes;
  - the truth lock is clean on both halves (the code check and the auditor).

  If any edit changed the letter after the critic scored it (the humanizer, the lint fix or the truth fix), the critic scores the final text again.

  Anything else is skipped, and the reason is recorded in the pipeline log, `applications.reason` and the quality report.

  `loadPacket()` and `packetForJob()` are what the form engine, the API and the email channel apply with. If the owner edited the letter or subject in the studio after writing, they re-run the lint and the code truth lock on the edited words, and return null if those fail.

  Caveat: the v1 `sendByEmail` path reads `applications` directly. A skipped application carries a high-severity "Quality gate" issue, so the v1 hunt's fact-lock check holds it back. A08 should send through `loadPacket`.
- ✅ **Voice-bank adaptation is verifiable.** Each row in `letter_variants.passages_used` stores the passages the text *measurably* reuses: at least 3 shared content trigrams each, out of the passages Claude claimed. The lint requires at least 2. `style_tags` also carries `passage:<id>`, `strategy:` and `len:`.
- ✅ **The CV PDF round-trips through text extraction with every section intact.** The selfcheck extracts the rendered PDF with `unpdf`. It finds every heading (Summary, Skills, Currently learning, Experience, Projects, Education) in reading order, plus the name, email, phone, summary, every role, employer, bullet, project line, skill and degree. The letter PDF is checked the same way.
- ✅ **The bandit updates from outcomes.** It was tested with 60 synthetic `outcomes` rows. Arm posteriors update; a rejection counts as a reply but not a win; choices favour the winning strategy and length (>75%) while exploring 20% ± 3% of the time.

## What I built (`server/writer/`)

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `index.ts` | The contract surface, with the stub names and signatures kept: `writeApplication(jobId, campaignId)`, `answerQuestion(jobId, question, opts)`, `draftFollowUp(applicationId)`. It also re-exports `loadPacket`, `packetForJob`, `loadVariants`, `banditStats`, the lint, the truth check and the humanizer rules. |
| `pipeline.ts` | The orchestrator, `writeApplicationRun`. It moves the job selected → writing → written, or to skipped with the reason, always through `transition()`. A regenerate goes from written, rehearsed, needs_you, failed or skipped back to selected first. A retryable error (budget, rate limit, offline, truncated) returns the job to `selected` with `attempts + 1`; any other error marks it `failed`. Jobs that are filling, verified or submitted are refused. Concurrent calls for one job share a single run. |
| `context.ts` | Loads the job, `jobs.match` (MatchResult, including `proofKind`), the master profile (it syncs the CV into facts first if the profile predates the fact store) and the research via `researchForJob`. A research failure only logs; the letters carry on without hooks. Also renders the shared prompt blocks. The candidate block (verbatim history, every active fact with its id, the learning list, the voice bank and the fingerprint) is the cached system prefix for every writer task. |
| `evidence.ts` | Steps 1 to 3 (task `evidence`): decode, hooks and the evidence map. Code then disposes of Claude's proposal: unknown fact ids are dropped; a direct or transferable claim with no real fact becomes `learning` if the skill is on the list, otherwise `omit`; a hook whose URL the research never read is dropped. Every adjustment is recorded. |
| `cv.ts` + `cvSchema.ts` | Step 4 (task `write_cv`). `sanitizeCv` pins name, contact, employers, titles, locations, dates and education to the source. It drops any skill, project or certification no fact backs, and moves learning-list skills into "Currently learning". `fitToPage` trims the least relevant lines until the rendered PDF measures 1 page (under 6 years of experience) or 2. |
| `letters.ts` | Steps 5, 10 and 12 (task `write_letter`): three variants (hook, proof, story) built by editing voice-bank passages, five subject lines, the outreach note and the follow-up. Also `reviseLetters` (the critic's demands, applied once), `fixTexts` (truth-lock repairs) and `subjectProblems` (under 70 characters; no clickbait, all-caps words, emoji or "!"). |
| `critic.ts` | Step 6 (task `critic`): a skeptical senior hiring manager scores specificity, evidence, voice, clarity, the ask and AI tells, lists the edits it demands, and picks the subject line. In code, the overall score may not exceed the sub-score mean + 0.5, and any sub-score under 6 caps it at 7.5. The bar is 8. |
| `humanizer.ts` | The rule set: 17 rules, paraphrased from Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" with attribution (CC BY-SA; no prose copied). It covers significance inflation, copula avoidance, promotional tone, vague attribution, AI vocabulary (every word the brief lists, plus more), "passionate", AI-editing transitions ("Additionally,", "Notably," and so on, from arXiv 2608.27855), negative parallelisms, formulaic openers and closers, hedging (stock phrases plus density above 2), sycophancy and chatbot residue, markdown, Title Case headings and placeholders. I checked blader/humanizer (MIT) and copied nothing from it. |
| `humanize.ts` | Step 7 (task `humanize`). Claude returns find/replace edits; **code applies only edits that sit inside a flagged sentence**, so nothing outside the offending spans can change. The same function performs the lint's single targeted rewrite. |
| `lint.ts` | Step 8, all in code, each check reporting a measured value and a target (details below). `lintShort` runs the subset that suits answers, notes and subject lines. |
| `truth.ts` + `lock.ts` | Step 9. `codeTruth` extends the v1 codeAudit (details below); `truthLock` runs the code check together with the auditor (task `audit`). An auditor that can't run throws, so an unaudited packet is never treated as clean. On a high-severity issue: one rewrite (CV and/or texts), a re-audit, then skip if still failing. |
| `answers.ts` | Step 11 (task `answer_q`). "Why us", "why this role" and "tell us about a project" are pre-written with every packet, each through the short lint and then the full truth lock. `answerQuestion` serves those three without a Claude call, and writes anything else from the stored evidence map through the short lint and the code truth lock: one rewrite, then null. With `options`, the value is always one of them exactly. |
| `followup.ts` | `draftFollowUp(applicationId)` returns the gated follow-up stored with the packet, under a `Re:` subject. If the application has no stored follow-up, it writes one through the same gates. Null when nothing passes. |
| `bandit.ts` | Step 14: Thompson sampling, as two Beta-Bernoulli bandits (strategy, and length band: short 180–215 words, medium 205–250, long 240–280), with 20% uniform exploration. The length is picked before the letters are written; the strategy is picked among letters that cleared the bar *and* sit within 1 point of the best. |
| `packet.ts` | Step 13: persistence. Writes `applications` (the v1 columns plus `campaign_id`, `variant_id`, `reason`, and the writer's working in `notes.writer`) and `letter_variants` (text, passages_used, critic, lint, style_tags, chosen). Renders the PDFs into `data/packets/<applicationId>/`. Also `loadPacket`, `packetForJob` and the re-gate of studio edits. |
| `choose.ts` | Switches the packet to another variant (studio). The same gates apply: critic ≥ 8, a lint pass now, and the full truth lock. |
| `quality.ts`, `report.ts` | The read models for the routes and the report. |
| `prompts.ts` | Every writer prompt. `TAILOR_RULES` (the shared alignment doctrine and truth lock) and `FACT_AUDITOR` are re-exported from `server/ai/prompts.ts` under their v1 names, and `SCORING_RUBRIC` is untouched. |
| `fixtures.ts`, `recorded.ts`, `record-fixtures.ts` | The recorded scenario, the hand-written Claude responses and the recorder (see Testing). |

### The lint (each check a pass/fail with a measured value)

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `length` | 180–280 body words (greeting and sign-off excluded) |
| `burstiness` | sentence-length SD ≥ 0.8 × the voice-bank fingerprint's |
| `lexical_diversity` | MATTR (window 50, same as A03's fingerprint) within ±15% of the candidate's. AI text runs high on lexical diversity (arXiv 2608.27855) |
| `contractions` | within ±50% of the fingerprint (absolute floor ±0.006) |
| `nominalizations` | ≤ 1.75 × the voice bank's rate + 1.5 per 100 words (Biber f_14, over-used by instruction-tuned models; arXiv 2604.14111) |
| `banned_phrases` | 0 humanizer hits |
| `formatting` | no markdown, Title Case headings or placeholders |
| `em_dashes` | ≤ 1 |
| `rule_of_three` | no "a, b and c" triads of short lowercase items. Lists of named tools and numbers are not flagged |
| `no_writing_to`, `no_excited_to_apply`, `no_passionate` | as named |
| `closing_summary` | the last paragraph has no stock summary phrase, and its final sentence does not recycle ≥ 60% of its content words from the letter |
| `specific_opening` | the first sentence names the company, the role or a hook term |
| `voice_adaptation` | ≥ 2 voice-bank passages reused |

### The truth lock (code half; every catch is high severity)

- Figures: digits, and number words followed by a unit, that appear in no fact. The employer's own numbers are allowed only when the sentence attributes them to the employer.
- Years of experience above the profile's.
- Scope inflation: "led", "managed", "headed", "spearheaded", "oversaw", "supervised", "directed" or "architected" when no fact uses that verb.
- Self-described seniority that no source title supports.
- An employer named in prose next to an employment cue that is not a source employer.
- In prose, a tool from a curated lexicon of 130 terms, or one of the posting's keywords, claimed as the candidate's without a fact behind it. Naming the employer's stack ("your OpenTelemetry setup") is fine. A learning-list skill is fine only with learning framing, and an admitted gap ("I haven't used…") is fine.
- In the CV:
  - an employer not in the source;
  - an inflated title (the CV title may drop words from the source title, never add any);
  - changed dates;
  - a skill no fact backs;
  - a gap skill listed as a skill;
  - a "Currently learning" item not on the learning list (a `queued` item does not count);
  - a certification or degree not in the source;
  - a changed name.
- An evidence-map claim that cites no real fact.

## Routes (all under the UI session guard)

| Method & path | Body / query | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `/api/writer/applications` | `?limit=&status=written\|skipped&campaignId=` | `{runs: RunSummary[], totals}`: critic, lint, truth, strategy, length, skip reason |
| GET `/api/writer/applications/:id` | | quality detail: the writer notes (evidence map, steps, subjects, short answers, gates), variants, issues, letter, CV |
| GET `/api/writer/applications/:id/variants` | | `{variants}`: text, critic, lint, passages used, style tags, chosen |
| POST `/api/writer/applications/:id/choose` | `{variantId}` | switches the letter if it clears all gates (spends one audit call); 422 `GATE_*` otherwise |
| POST `/api/writer/applications/:id/follow-up` | | `{subject, body}`, or 404 |
| GET `/api/writer/applications/:id/cv.pdf`, `/letter.pdf` | | the rendered PDFs (only files inside `data/packets/`) |
| GET `/api/writer/jobs/:jobId/packet` | | `{packet}` (ApplicationPacket), or 404 |
| POST `/api/writer/jobs/:jobId/regenerate` | `{campaignId?, instructions?}` | `{applicationId, packet}` or `{applicationId, skipped}` (spends AI budget) |
| POST `/api/writer/jobs/:jobId/answer` | `{question, maxChars?, options?}` | `{answer: Answered\|null, lint, truth, attempts}` |
| GET `/api/writer/bandit` | | arm stats (alpha, beta, mean, n) by strategy and length, outcome count, explore rate |
| POST `/api/writer/lint` | `{text, kind?: letter\|short, company?, role?, maxChars?}` | `{lint, fingerprint}`: "check my edit" in the studio |
| GET `/api/writer/meta` | | the critic bar, length bands, explore rate, and the humanizer rules with attribution |

I smoke-tested the real server on a temporary data dir: it boots, and the routes answer behind the guard.

## How to run and test

- `npm run selfcheck -- a04` runs A04's 62 checks offline (replay mode, hash embeddings). The full `npm run selfcheck` passes.
- `npm run writer:report` lists the last 20 runs. Other options:
  - `--limit N`
  - `--skipped`
  - `--campaign <id>`
  - `--json`
  - `--detail <applicationId>`: steps, evidence map with framings and fact ids, each variant's critic, lint and passages, every lint check with its value and target, truth issues, code corrections and the letter.

  It reads `BUREAU_DATA_DIR` (default `./data`) and never calls Claude.
- **Recordings:**
  - Run `npx tsx server/writer/record-fixtures.ts` (or `--preview` to only list label, task and hash). It seeds the scenario in a throwaway database and runs the real pipeline with a fake client that saves the hand-written responses from `server/writer/recorded.ts` under their replay hashes.
  - Re-run it after changing any writer prompt, a prompt block, the scenario or a canned response. Otherwise replay fails with `REPLAY_MISSING` and the hash.
  - The scenario's ids and timestamps are all fixed, and the bandit runs on seed 3, so hashes are stable.
- **The fixture story** (11 recordings): a junior backend developer with 6 voice passages applies to a stretch role, Backend Engineer, Payments, at a fictional fintech. Go, PostgreSQL and ledgers are direct; AWS and Kubernetes are on the learning list; observability is transferable; years and Kafka are omitted.
  - The evidence step proposes a hook from an unread URL and a non-existent fact id; code drops both.
  - The CV lists Kubernetes as a skill; code moves it to Currently learning.
  - Two of the three letters have flaws ("I am writing to apply", a summary closer). The critic demands fixes and the revision applies them.
  - The bandit picks the story letter. The humanizer removes "crucial" (a single in-span edit).
  - The lint and the truth lock pass, the critic re-scores the edited letter at 8.6, and the PDFs render.
- **What else the tests cover:**
  - Every lint rule, each failing on a purpose-built letter.
  - Every truth-lock catch in the brief: invented metric, invented skill, gap skill listed as a skill, inflated title. Also changed dates, invented employer, scope, years, seniority, certification and evidence-map claims.
  - Edits outside the flagged spans are rejected.
  - The critic caps; subject lines.
  - End to end, with an injected fake client: critic under 8 → skip; still under 8 after the demands → skip; an unfixable lint failure → skip; a fixable one → written; an invented metric the rewrite doesn't remove → skip; one it does → written (re-audited and re-scored); an auditor-only finding → skip; a final critic score under 8 → skip; fewer than 2 voice passages → skip.
  - Retryable versus fatal errors; refusal of unselected jobs; regenerate; choosing another variant; the re-gate of studio edits.
  - Answers (pre-written, replayed free-form, failing, options) and the follow-up.
  - The bandit, the routes through `inject`, and the report.

## Known limits

- **Live quality is unmeasured.** Every recording is hand-written. Real Opus letters, critic calibration (does Opus give 8+ only to letters a hiring manager would act on?) and the auditor's recall are untested until Phase 3. Use `npm run writer:report -- --detail` on real runs.
- **Lint thresholds come from one fictional voice bank** of about 500 words. MATTR on a 200-word letter is noisy, and a voice bank under about 300 words gives a shaky fingerprint. Of the 2608.27855 markers, entropy is not measured separately; the TTR band covers lexical diversity, its strongest correlate. The short-sample markers in 2507.00838 (sentence count, punctuation share) come from encyclopedic text and were not adopted.
- **The code truth lock is lexical.** A number counts as backed if it appears in *any* fact; context isn't checked, which is the auditor's job. A tool outside the lexicon and outside the posting's keywords can slip past the code check (the auditor still reads it). The employer-in-prose check needs an employment cue ("worked at…"). Number words are recognised only with a unit noun.
- **Rule of three:** triads of pronoun-led clauses ("it shipped, it balanced, and nobody lost a sale") are deliberately not flagged. They are the candidate's own rhythm, and flagging them would fight the voice bank.
- **Title Case heading rule:** it can fire on a three-or-more-word Title Case line inside prose.
- **Owner edits** are re-gated by the lint and the code truth lock, not by the auditor or the critic. The critic score shown is the gated draft's.
- **The bandit** treats strategy and length as independent, applies no time decay and uses no context (role category, ATS). A reply that is not a rejection counts as a win.
- **PDFs use the standard Helvetica font (WinAnsi).** Latin-1 names render; Urdu or other non-Latin script would not. Embedding a Unicode font would fix it but needs a font file in the repo.
- **v1 hunt cost:** on a gate failure the v1 hunt calls `draftApplication` twice, which is now two full pipeline runs. A08 replaces the hunt.

## Follow-ups for other agents

- **A08:**
  - For each `selected` job, `await writeApplication(jobId, campaignId)` returns a packet or `{skipped}`; the pipeline is already moved.
  - A thrown error leaves the job at `selected` (retryable; `attempts` counts) or `failed`.
  - Send only what `loadPacket` / `packetForJob` returns.
  - The writer spends about 10 Opus calls per job (evidence, CV, letters, two critic passes, revise, humanize, answers, audit, final critic). `taskCost()` already has estimates.
- **A05:**
  - `packetForJob(jobId)` gives `cvPdfPath`, `letterPdfPath`, `coverLetter` and `shortAnswers`.
  - For other long-form fields, call `answerQuestion(jobId, label, {maxChars, options})`.
  - When it returns null, call `recordUnknown`.
- **A07:** the packet and answer endpoints map onto `loadPacket` and `answerQuestion`. Contract request 2 adds `variantId`, `strategy` and `cvPages` if you want them.
- **A09:** fill `outcomes` (`replied`, `reply_class`); the bandit reads it on the next application. `draftFollowUp(applicationId)` returns `{subject, body}` or null.
- **A10:**
  - Show the routes above (quality per application, variants with "use this letter", bandit stats, regenerate with notes, the lint box).
  - The v1 applications list now contains `status = 'skipped'` with `reason`.
  - The v1 "Rewrite with notes" button already runs the v2 writer.
- **A11:** the scenario (`server/writer/fixtures.ts`), the canned responses and the recorder are reusable for e2e. A written fixture job can be produced with `seedScenario()` plus `writeApplicationRun(JOB_ID, CAMPAIGN_ID, {rng: seededRng(SEED)})` in replay mode.
- **Lead:** the contract requests in `docs/build/requests/A04.md` are optional.
